I have signed hundreds of drill records. But I have watched only about a third of those drills. That is the problem. On paper, we have a lifeboat drill every month, and every person on board has a muster station. In practice, some drills take eleven minutes, and then everyone goes back to work. Nobody learns anything. Now I want to see a real drill. I want somebody to notice when the list is wrong. And I want every near miss written down, even when nothing happened. Nobody is punished for an accident that did not happen. That is why people report near misses honestly.
Seldom is a lifeboat drill longer than fifteen minutes.
Never had the new cadet seen a real emergency.
Not only does the ISM Code ask for procedures, but it also asks for training.
Not until the alarm sounded did the crew go to the muster station.
The master is the officer in command of a merchant ship.
Every officer needs a valid certificate under STCW.
